documents.title: Diabetes / CKD Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back after the holidays. Less walking with the ice; using the mall track twice a week instead. Fasting readings 140-165. Denies lows, chest pain, dyspnea, ankle swelling, urinary symptoms.
O: vitals per flowsheet. Alert, comfortable. RRR. CTA bilaterally. Feet: skin intact both soles, no ulceration.
A/P: T2DM on glipizide, CKD 3b, HTN. A1c and BMP drawn. Continue meds. Eye exam due in March, he has it booked. 3 months.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Annual diabetic eye exam - report to primary care
Patient: Frederick Esposito, DOB 11/15/1959
Seen 3/12/2024. Allergy: penicillin.
Best corrected acuity 20/25 each eye. Pupils dilated. Intraocular lens stable and clear. Retina: no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization in either eye. Macula flat and dry.
Assessment: type 2 diabetes, no diabetic retinopathy.
Return one year.

documents.title: Chronic Disease Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up. Feels well. Eye exam in March without retinopathy. Morning sugars mostly in the 140s. Back outside walking.

Exam: BP charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Extremities warm, no swelling. Feet without breakdown.

Plan: same three medicines for sugar and pressure, statin and aspirin. Labs today. Physical in September.

documents.title: Spot on bottom of my foot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I've been finding a little wet spot on my right sock for about a week. There's a sore on the bottom of the foot, doesn't hurt much. My wife looked at it and said call you. Should I come in?

documents.title: RE: Spot on bottom of my foot
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, I'd like to look at it tomorrow. The front desk will text you a morning time. Keep it covered with a clean dry bandage and try to stay off it tonight.

conditions.label: Diabetic foot ulcer, right plantar surface

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-day visit - right foot
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen same day after last night's portal message. Noticed drainage on his right sock about a week ago; found a sore on the sole. Little pain. No fever or chills. No injury he remembers.

Exam: afebrile, vitals charted. Right foot: plantar ulcer approx 1.2 x 1.0 cm with a clean pink base. No surrounding redness or warmth, no purulent drainage, no odor. No streaking up the foot. Pedal pulses palpable. Left foot intact.

A/P: diabetic foot ulcer, right plantar surface, uninfected. Cleaned and dressed in office. Urgent podiatry referral for debridement and offloading. Daily dressing changes, keep weight off it as much as possible. Reviewed warning signs - spreading redness, swelling, fever, pus - and to text me right away if any of those.

documents.title: Podiatry consultation
documents.author: podiatry
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PODIATRY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Re: Frederick Esposito  DOB 11/15/1959
Date of service: 6/27/2024
Referred by primary care for a right plantar wound.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis).
Meds: glipizide, metoprolol, lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin.

History: 64-year-old with type 2 diabetes and stage 3 CKD; wound on the right sole first noticed about three weeks ago.
Exam: DP and PT pulses palpable bilaterally. Right plantar foot: full-thickness ulcer 1.2 x 1.0 x 0.3 cm, granular base, no exposed bone or tendon, no probe to bone. Periwound with mild callus, no erythema or fluctuance. Left foot intact.
Procedure: sharp excisional debridement of callus and nonviable tissue, tolerated well.
Impression: diabetic foot ulcer, right plantar surface, no signs of infection.
Plan: offloading walker boot dispensed; dressing changes daily; follow-up every 2-4 weeks. Glucose control discussed.
Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Bandages
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The foot doctor wants me doing dressings every day and I'm going through the supplies fast. Pharmacy says insurance would cover them with an order. Can you send one? The boot is a pain but I'm wearing it.

documents.title: RE: Bandages
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Frederick, the doctor signed an order for daily wound dressing supplies and we faxed it to your pharmacy. They should have it by tomorrow. Glad you're sticking with the boot.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical, age 64.

Since last year: right plantar diabetic ulcer since June, under podiatry every few weeks, debrided, in an offloading boot. Says it is 'shrinking slowly.' No fever. Otherwise well. Less walking because of the boot. PHQ-2 1 (a bit fed up with the boot), no depressed mood.

Meds: glipizide 5 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg. Allergy: penicillin - anaphylaxis.

Exam: NAD. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Right foot: dressing removed - small plantar ulcer, clean base, no surrounding erythema or drainage; boot back on. Left foot intact. No edema.

Assessment/Plan:
1. T2DM - A1c today.
2. Right plantar ulcer - podiatry following; keep offloading.
3. CKD 3b / HTN - CMP, urine albumin today. Meds unchanged.
4. Lipids today on atorvastatin 40.
5. Lung screening CT ordered for October.
6. Vaccines: flu, COVID and RSV at an October nurse visit.
Next visit December.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three vaccines today per PCP order: high-dose flu (L arm), 2024-25 COVID (R arm), RSV (L arm, separate site). RSV recommended given age and diabetes/CKD. Screening negative. Observed 15 minutes without reaction. Walking boot on right foot, gait steady.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
OUTSIDE IMAGING CENTER - LDCT LUNG SCREENING, ANNUAL
Comparison: 10/24/2023 and 10/18/2022.
Technique: Low-dose CT of the chest, no IV contrast.
Findings: Lungs without nodules. No airspace disease. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Mediastinum and hila normal. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
Requisition allergies: penicillin.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Next annual LDCT in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT 2024
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Third screening CT negative. Message sent to patient. Next due fall 2025.

documents.title: Podiatry follow-up
documents.author: podiatry
documents.body:
PODIATRY PROGRESS LETTER
Patient: Frederick Esposito  DOB 11/15/1959  Visit 11/12/2024
Allergies: penicillin.
Right plantar ulcer now 0.8 x 0.6 cm, shallow, granular base, no drainage, no erythema, no undermining. Pulses palpable. Debrided rim of callus.
Assessment: diabetic foot ulcer right plantar surface, improving, not infected.
Plan: continue offloading boot and daily dressings; return 3 months, sooner for any change.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Just turned 65 and now on Medicare. Foot ulcer smaller per podiatry last month; still in the boot. No redness or fever. Sugars 140s-170s in the mornings. No lows.

Exam: vitals charted. Cardiac regular. Lungs clear. Right foot: small plantar ulcer, clean, no surrounding redness; dressing replaced.

A/P
- T2DM: A1c, BMP today. No changes.
- Diabetic foot ulcer, right sole: podiatry following, next visit February.
- CKD 3b/HTN: stable regimen.
- One-time abdominal aortic ultrasound now that he is 65 with a smoking history - ordered.
Next visit spring.
